body.statement:
Let \(S\) and \(T\) be standard Borel spaces and let \((Z,W)\) be an \(S\times T\)-valued random element.  There is a Borel probability kernel \(K:S\times\mathcal B(T)\to[0,1]\) such that, writing \(P_Z\) for the law of \(Z\),
\[
 \Pr\{Z\in B,W\in C\}=\int_B K(z,C)\,P_Z(\mathrm dz)
\]
for every Borel \(B\subseteq S\) and \(C\subseteq T\).

source.verbatim_statement: Let X be a standard Borel space, Y a measurable space, and X and Y corresponding random variables. Then there exists a kernel μ from Y to X satisfying P(X ∈ B | Y) = μ(Y,B) for Borel B, and this kernel is unique almost surely with respect to the law of Y.

attestation.note: Main verified the normalized Theorem 6.3 statement through an exact public scholarly restatement (Schrott 2021, Theorem A.27, explicitly citing Kallenberg 2002 Theorem 6.3) and confirmed the cited 2002 chapter/edition and conditional-distribution scope on SpringerLink.
